walkthrough:
Integrate $y$ with respect to $x$ using the reverse power rule:
$$\int y\,dx = \frac{(4x + 1)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 4} + \frac{9(4x + 1)^{1/2}}{\frac{1}{2} \times 4} + c$$
$$\int y\,dx = \frac{1}{6}(4x + 1)^{3/2} + \frac{9}{2}\sqrt{4x + 1} + c$$

ai_rubric.Differentiation and Integration: Differentiates correctly to $\frac{2}{\sqrt{4x+1}} - \frac{18}{(4x+1)^{3/2}}$ (B3). Integrates to $\frac{1}{6}(4x+1)^{3/2} + \frac{9}{2}\sqrt{4x+1} + c$ (B3).

hints: Solve for $x = 2$ and evaluate $y = 6$ to give $M(2, 6)$.
walkthrough:
Set the first derivative equal to zero to find the coordinates of minimum point $M$:
$$\frac{2}{\sqrt{4x + 1}} - \frac{18}{(4x + 1)^{3/2}} = 0 \implies \frac{2}{\sqrt{4x + 1}} = \frac{18}{(4x + 1)^{3/2}}$$

Evaluate the $y$-coordinate on the curve:
$$y = \sqrt{4(2) + 1} + \frac{9}{\sqrt{4(2) + 1}} = \sqrt{9} + \frac{9}{\sqrt{9}} = 3 + 3 = 6$$
$$\text{Coordinates of } M: \quad (2, 6)$$

skill_tags: Finding an Area Between a Line and a Curve

hints: Subtract the rectangle area under $y = 6$ from $0$ to $2$ ($12$) to obtain $\frac{4}{3}$.
walkthrough:
Evaluate the definite integral under the curve from $x = 0$ to the $x$-coordinate of $M$ ($x = 2$):
$$\text{Area}_{\text{under curve}} = \left[ \frac{1}{6}(4x + 1)^{3/2} + \frac{9}{2}\sqrt{4x + 1} \right]_0^2$$
$$F(2) = \frac{1}{6}(27) + \frac{9}{2}(3) = 4.5 + 13.5 = 18$$
$$F(0) = \frac{1}{6}(1) + \frac{9}{2}(1) = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{9}{2} = \frac{28}{6} = \frac{14}{3} = 4\frac{2}{3}$$
$$\text{Area}_{\text{under curve}} = 18 - \frac{14}{3} = \frac{40}{3} = 13\frac{1}{3}$$

Calculate the area of the rectangle beneath the horizontal tangent line $y = 6$ over $[0, 2]$:
$$\text{Area}_{\text{rectangle}} = 6 \times 2 = 12$$

Subtract the rectangle area from the curve area to find the shaded region:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = \text{Area}_{\text{under curve}} - \text{Area}_{\text{rectangle}} = \frac{40}{3} - 12 = \frac{4}{3} = 1\frac{1}{3} \quad (\approx 1.33)$$

ai_rubric.Area Between Curves: Applies limits $0$ to $2$ to integral to get $13\frac{1}{3}$ (M1, DM1). Subtracts rectangle area $12$ to obtain shaded area $\frac{4}{3}$ (A1).
